study type: Matched maternal-infant preterm cohort study (cross-sectional analysis)
exposure: Viral presence (adenovirus, anellovirus, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, enterovirus, human herpesvirus 6, parechovirus, parvovirus B19)
Viral load in maternal plasma/whole blood
Viral presence/load in infant cord blood
cohort: The study included 56 matched maternal and premature infant dyads.
finding: Viral detection was more common in maternal samples (52%) than in infant cord blood (7%), and no significant association was found between maternal viral presence or load and histologic chorioamnionitis, spontaneous preterm labor, or pre-eclampsia.
cross-section timing: Samples were collected from mothers and infant cord blood at the time of preterm birth.
